facts.text: Camperdown was named after the Battle of Camperdown, a naval victory celebrated by Governor William Bligh when he granted the land.
The suburb hosts the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital, one of Sydney’s oldest hospitals, originally built on a former racecourse opened in 1827.
The University of Sydney’s first buildings, designed by Edmund Blacket, were erected in Camperdown in 1850, making the area a historic academic hub.
Converted warehouses and factories across Camperdown tell the story of its past as a major industrial centre of Sydney.
Camperdown’s streets feature Victorian terraced housing, many single‑storey terraces that echo the suburb’s 19th‑century residential character.
The Heritage Centre in Camperdown opens Tuesdays and the first Sunday of each month, offering history talks and a glimpse into local heritage.
